name: Data Collection Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday data collection work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical data collection tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday data collection work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical data collection tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate data collection outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. State assumptions about data collection explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
3. Re-check edge cases relevant to data collection (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
4. Document any non-obvious data collection decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. When data collection guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. When data collection decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
7. Prefer the simplest data collection approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. Keep data collection changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
9. Before starting data collection work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated data collection concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not apply generic data collection advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting data collection assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new data collection abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these data collection guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
